q7.answer: Each provider client receives the secret provider when it is built and calls get('payments'), get('email') or get('geocoding') on every request, so it reads the holder's current value rather than a copy made at construction. The 5-minute refresh swaps the whole holder record at once, and a request takes its snapshot when it starts, so the next request after a refresh uses the new key.

q8.answer: The version-id lines written at startup and on each change go to the central log service, and the security on-call queries it for each pod's lines and records the result in the migration record, confirming every pod logs the new version id for all three keys. This check is manual unless someone automates it, and it also requires that no old-ReplicaSet pod remains, provider error rates are at baseline, and the bake period has run before revocation.

q9.answer: The order is: set store access (step 2), rotate each key at its provider while the old key stays valid (step 4), copy the new keys into the prod store and check them with a read-only provider call (step 5), then merge the code switch and the removal of api_key lines from config/app.yaml as one change and build the image (step 6), then roll out to production (step 7). Removal of keys from the committed file is therefore part of the same merge as the switch to store reads, and both come before the rollout and the revocation of old keys (step 11).

q10.answer: make run loads the dev keys from orders-api/dev/* using the developer's own dev identity, which has no prod access, and holds them in memory only. If the developer has no dev access or the dev store is down, make run-offline starts the app with stub provider clients that need no key.

q11.answer: The app retries the store read, then exits with a non-zero code and logs an error naming the missing secret, never its value. The pod never becomes ready, the cluster restarts it with backoff, and old pods keep serving; the plan sets no time limit on this loop, and whether a retry is one attempt plus 3 retries or 3 total attempts is still open (open question 4).
